title: Unified Internal Dashboard Standardization
business: Internal enterprise teams managing fragmented legacy admin panels.
problem: Teams struggle with inconsistent UI patterns and rigid third-party component libraries that prevent deep customization, leading to high maintenance overhead when design requirements evolve.
solution: By adopting shadcn/ui, the organization moves from consuming opaque NPM packages to owning the component source code, allowing developers to modify Tailwind CSS classes and React logic directly within their local project structure.
steps: Initialize the project using the shadcn/ui CLI to create the components directory.
Add specific components like Button, Card, and Table to the local registry.
Modify the source code of the installed components to match internal brand guidelines.
Utilize the shared composable interface to build complex dashboard views.
Commit the component source code directly to the application repository.
outcome: A consistent, fully owned design system that allows for rapid, granular UI updates without fighting against external library abstractions.
limitation: Because the code is copied locally, upstream updates to the original shadcn/ui library are not automatically applied, requiring manual synchronization or careful tracking of component changes.
